root_cause.text: The driver assumes the FIFO entry count from hardware is always a multiple of the number of enabled scan elements, but the sensor fills the FIFO one sample at a time, so when the count is not a multiple, the driver reads more entries than actually present, potentially reading stale or out-of-bounds data.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that "the sensor fills the FIFO one sample at a time, even when more than one channel is enabled. Therefore, the number of entries reported by the FIFO status registers may not be a multiple of N; if this number is not a multiple, the number of entries read from the FIFO may exceed the number of entries actually present." The patch adds `fifo_entries = rounddown(fifo_entries, st->fifo_set_size);` to fix this.

candidates.rationale: The loop condition uses fifo_entries directly without ensuring it is a multiple of fifo_set_size, causing the driver to attempt to read more entries than actually present when fifo_entries is not a multiple.
This function call reads a block of data from the FIFO; when invoked with insufficient remaining entries (due to the loop assumption), it may read stale or out-of-bounds data.

The buffer index i is incremented by fifo_set_size each iteration; when the total number of FIFO entries is not a multiple, the index can point to memory beyond the valid FIFO data, leading to an out-of-bounds read.

This error check only handles failure of the register read, but does not detect or mitigate the scenario where the read completes successfully but reads more entries than available due to the assumption of a multiple.

By returning IRQ_HANDLED unconditionally after the loop, the driver does not verify that the number of read entries matches the expected multiple, leaving the buffer potentially partially filled with stale data.

vuln_statements.explanation: The loop condition uses 'fifo_entries' directly, assuming it is always a multiple of 'fifo_set_size'. When it is not, the loop attempts to read more entries than actually present, potentially reading stale or out-of-bounds data.

This call reads a block of data from the FIFO of size 'fifo_set_size'. When the loop condition allows a read with insufficient remaining entries, it may read stale or out-of-bounds data from the FIFO.

The index 'i' is incremented by 'fifo_set_size' each iteration. When 'fifo_entries' is not a multiple of 'fifo_set_size', the index can point beyond the valid FIFO data, leading to an out-of-bounds read into the buffer.

This error check only handles failures of the register read (e.g., I2C/SPI errors). It does not detect or mitigate the scenario where the read completes successfully but reads more entries than available due to the non-multiple count.

The function unconditionally returns IRQ_HANDLED after the loop, without verifying that the number of read entries matches the expected multiple of 'fifo_set_size'. This leaves the buffer potentially partially filled with stale data and the system unaware of the inconsistency.
